A part is fabricated by depositing successive layers of a model material that contains sinterable metal particles and a first binder. The deposited layers define the geometry of the part, including a region that surrounds and forms a hole.

Within this hole, a first support structure is also deposited in layers using the same model material. Because the support structure is made from the same metal-particle-containing material as the part, it is capable of undergoing substantially the same densification behavior during later thermal processing.

To separate the support structure from the surrounding part, release layers are deposited within the hole both above and below the first support structure. These release layers are formed from a release material that includes ceramic powder dispersed in a second binder. Thus, the first release layer is positioned on one side of the support structure, and the second release layer is positioned on the opposite side, creating interfaces that separate the support structure from adjacent portions of the part.

Together, the part, the first and second release layers, and the first support structure form a multipiece assembly. Although these elements are built together during the deposition process, the release layers are designed to prevent permanent bonding between the part and the support structure.

During sintering, the metal particles in both the part and the support structure densify in a generally uniform manner. At the same time, the binder components are removed, and the release material is converted into loose ceramic powder. Because the support structure densifies similarly to the part, it provides mechanical support within the hole during sintering and helps reduce or prevent distortion, deformation, or collapse of the hole. After sintering, the loose ceramic powder and the support structure can be removed, leaving the part with a more accurately maintained hole geometry.
outputs.L4:
A method is provided for producing a metal or metal-matrix part by three-dimensional printing while preserving the shape of an internal opening, passage, bore, or other hole during later thermal processing. In the method, a printable model material is deposited layer by layer to form the body of the part. The model material includes metal particles combined with a binder, so that the printed “green” part has the desired shape but has not yet been densified.

When the part includes a hole or other unsupported feature, a support structure is printed inside the hole during the same build process. The support structure is made from a material that is compositionally and dimensionally compatible with the model material, for example the same or a closely matching metal-particle/binder material. Because the support and the surrounding part are made from matching or similar materials, they shrink and densify at substantially the same rate during sintering. This uniform densification helps prevent the hole from collapsing, warping, becoming oval, or otherwise losing dimensional accuracy.

To make the support removable after sintering, release layers are printed between the support structure and the part. A lower release layer is deposited beneath the support, and an upper release layer is deposited above the support, so that the support is separated from the surrounding part at the relevant contact regions. These release layers contain ceramic powder or another material that does not sinter into a strong solid bond under the sintering conditions used for the metal-containing model material. The ceramic-powder release material may be deposited as a thin layer, coating, or interface region sufficient to prevent bonding between the support and the part.

After printing, the green assembly includes the part, the internal support, and the intervening release layers. The assembly may then undergo debinding to remove at least part of the binder, followed by sintering at a temperature suitable for densifying the metal particles. During sintering, the part and the internal support shrink together in a substantially coordinated manner. Because the support remains dimensionally compatible with the part throughout this process, it mechanically supports the hole and maintains the intended geometry of the opening.

At the same time, the ceramic-powder release layers do not densify into a rigid, bonded interface. Instead, they remain weak, friable, or powder-like after sintering. As a result, once the sintering operation is complete and the part has cooled, the support can be separated from the finished part. The loose release-layer material may be broken away, shaken out, blown out, washed out, brushed away, or otherwise removed, permitting the support to be extracted from the hole without damaging the surrounding sintered metal structure.

This approach allows complex metal parts with holes, channels, and other internal or partially enclosed features to be printed with improved dimensional control. The matching support material prevents distortion during the shrinkage associated with sintering, while the ceramic-powder release layers ensure that the support does not become permanently bonded to the part. The result is a sintered metal part having a more accurate and cleaner internal opening than would typically be obtained if the hole were left unsupported during densification.

“A method comprising” is a common phrase used in patent claims to introduce the steps of an invention. It signals that the claim is directed to a process or procedure, rather than a physical product or system. The word “comprising” is especially important because it is generally interpreted as open-ended. This means that the method includes the listed steps, but it may also include additional steps that are not specifically mentioned.

For example, a claim might begin: “A method comprising receiving data, processing the data, and displaying a result.” In this case, the method must include the steps of receiving, processing, and displaying. However, other actions—such as storing the data, encrypting it, or transmitting it to another device—may also be part of the method without avoiding the scope of the claim.

The phrase is widely used because it provides flexibility. It allows inventors to define the essential parts of their process while still covering variations and improvements that perform the same core function. In legal and technical writing, “a method comprising” helps establish the boundaries of protection for an invention and is often followed by a sequence of carefully drafted operational steps.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate patent-style language for a process involving layered deposition of metal-particle/binder model material and ceramic-powder release material to form a multipiece assembly with an internal support structure that densifies uniformly during sintering.
counterfactuals.output:
**Patent-Style Process Language**

In one embodiment, a method of fabricating a multipiece sinterable assembly comprises selectively depositing, in a layerwise manner, a model material comprising metal particles dispersed in a removable binder and a release material comprising ceramic powder dispersed in a removable binder. The model material is deposited in regions corresponding to a plurality of discrete article portions, and the release material is deposited in regions corresponding to interfaces between the article portions and to at least one internal support structure disposed within a cavity or spacing between the article portions. Successive layers are deposited to define a green multipiece assembly in which the article portions are physically supported relative to one another by the internal support structure during binder removal and sintering.

The release material is selected to be substantially non-sintering or less-sintering under sintering conditions effective to densify the metal particles of the model material. During thermal processing, the binder of the model material and the binder of the release material are removed, and the metal particles of the model material are sintered to form densified metal article portions. The ceramic powder of the release material remains substantially unconsolidated, friable, or otherwise separable from the densified metal article portions, thereby permitting removal of the release material after sintering to separate the article portions and expose surfaces previously adjacent the release material.

In certain embodiments, the internal support structure comprises a lattice, rib, column, web, honeycomb, gyroid, or other porous or cellular structure formed from the release material. The internal support structure is configured to provide mechanical support to overhanging, suspended, or mutually spaced regions of the model material while allowing shrinkage of the model material during sintering. The internal support structure may be dimensioned, patterned, or otherwise configured to reduce differential constraint on the article portions, such that the article portions densify substantially uniformly during sintering.

In some embodiments, the release material is deposited in a pattern that substantially surrounds at least a portion of the model material, fills a gap between adjacent model-material regions, or occupies an internal void of the green assembly. The release material may further define parting planes, clearance regions, sacrificial supports, removable cores, or internal channels. After sintering, the release material is removed by vibration, blasting, brushing, fluid flow, ultrasonic agitation, mechanical extraction, or a combination thereof.

In further embodiments, the metal particles comprise steel, stainless steel, tool steel, titanium, aluminum, nickel, cobalt, copper, bronze, refractory metal, superalloy, or an alloy thereof. The ceramic powder of the release material may comprise alumina, zirconia, silica, yttria, magnesia, mullite, silicon carbide, silicon nitride, boron nitride, or combinations thereof. The binder of the model material and the binder of the release material may be the same or different and may comprise a polymeric, wax, thermoplastic, photopolymeric, solvent-based, or thermally removable binder system.

**Example Independent Claim**

1. A method of making a multipiece metal assembly, the method comprising:  
 depositing a plurality of layers, each layer comprising selectively deposited portions of:  
 a model material comprising metal particles and a first removable binder; and  
 a release material comprising ceramic powder and a second removable binder;  
 wherein the selectively deposited portions of the model material define a plurality of separate green metal bodies, and wherein the selectively deposited portions of the release material define at least one release region between the separate green metal bodies and an internal support structure positioned to support at least one of the separate green metal bodies during subsequent thermal processing;  
 removing at least a portion of the first removable binder and the second removable binder;  
 sintering the metal particles of the model material to densify the separate green metal bodies into a plurality of densified metal parts; and  
 removing the release material from between the densified metal parts,  
 wherein the internal support structure is configured to permit substantially uniform shrinkage of the separate green metal bodies during sintering.

**Example Dependent Claims**

2. The method of claim 1, wherein the internal support structure comprises a lattice structure formed from the release material.

3. The method of claim 1, wherein the internal support structure comprises a plurality of spaced supports configured to contact one or more surfaces of the separate green metal bodies.

4. The method of claim 1, wherein the ceramic powder of the release material remains substantially unsintered during sintering of the metal particles.

5. The method of claim 1, wherein the release material is friable after sintering and is removable by mechanical agitation, fluid flow, blasting, brushing, or ultrasonic treatment.

6. The method of claim 1, wherein the release material defines a parting interface between adjacent densified metal parts.

7. The method of claim 1, wherein the release material defines a sacrificial core within an internal cavity of at least one of the separate green metal bodies.

8. The method of claim 1, wherein the internal support structure has an open-cell geometry to facilitate binder removal and release-material removal.

9. The method of claim 1, wherein the internal support structure is configured to reduce gravitational sag, warpage, or distortion of the separate green metal bodies during binder removal or sintering.

10. The method of claim 1, wherein the metal particles comprise stainless steel, tool steel, titanium alloy, nickel alloy, cobalt alloy, copper alloy, bronze, or combinations thereof.

11. The method of claim 1, wherein the ceramic powder comprises alumina, zirconia, silica, yttria, magnesia, mullite, silicon carbide, silicon nitride, boron nitride, or combinations thereof.

12. The method of claim 1, wherein the first removable binder and the second removable binder comprise thermoplastic binders that are deposited by material extrusion.

13. The method of claim 1, wherein the first removable binder and the second removable binder comprise photocurable binders that are deposited and cured layerwise.

14. The method of claim 1, wherein the separate green metal bodies are arranged in a nested, interlocking, stacked, or spaced configuration during sintering.

15. The method of claim 1, wherein the internal support structure is separated from the model material by one or more release gaps or interface regions formed from the release material.

16. The method of claim 1, wherein the internal support structure comprises a geometry selected to provide support while imposing less shrinkage constraint than a solid support body.

17. The method of claim 1, wherein sintering causes the separate green metal bodies to shrink by substantially the same shrinkage ratio in at least two orthogonal directions.

18. The method of claim 1, wherein the release material is deposited to compensate for predicted shrinkage of the model material during sintering.

19. The method of claim 1, wherein the multipiece metal assembly comprises a plurality of movable, separable, or mating metal components after removal of the release material.

20. The method of claim 1, wherein the release material is removed to yield a clearance between adjacent densified metal parts.

**Additional Apparatus/System Claim Language**

21. A green multipiece assembly for sintering, comprising:  
 a plurality of green metal bodies comprising metal particles in a removable binder; and  
 a ceramic-powder release structure comprising ceramic powder in a removable binder, the ceramic-powder release structure being disposed between at least two of the green metal bodies and comprising an internal support structure positioned to support the green metal bodies during binder removal or sintering;  
 wherein the ceramic-powder release structure is configured to remain separable from the green metal bodies after sintering of the metal particles.

22. The green multipiece assembly of claim 21, wherein the internal support structure comprises a porous lattice configured to accommodate shrinkage of the green metal bodies during sintering.

23. The green multipiece assembly of claim 21, wherein the ceramic-powder release structure defines one or more sacrificial supports, parting layers, removable cores, or clearance-forming regions.

**Specification-Style Description**

A build file may be generated from a digital model of a plurality of parts to be formed as a single green assembly. The build file may assign voxels, roads, pixels, or other deposition regions to either a metal-particle model material or a ceramic-powder release material. The model material may be assigned to regions corresponding to final metal components, while the release material may be assigned to temporary interface regions, separation regions, support regions, and internal support structures. The internal support structures may be generated automatically based on overhang angle, span distance, predicted shrinkage, predicted distortion, local part mass, or a combination thereof.

The model material and release material may be co-deposited using extrusion, jetting, binder jetting, vat photopolymerization, sheet lamination, powder deposition, or hybrid additive manufacturing techniques. In an extrusion embodiment, the model material and release material are each provided as flowable feedstocks containing particulate solids and thermoplastic binder systems. The materials are alternately or concurrently extruded to form each layer. After deposition of a layer, the layer may be cooled, cured, leveled, compacted, or otherwise conditioned before deposition of a subsequent layer.

Following layerwise fabrication, the green multipiece assembly is subjected to debinding. Debinding may include solvent debinding, catalytic debinding, thermal debinding, wicking, supercritical fluid extraction, or combinations thereof. The ceramic release material may provide venting paths or open porosity that facilitates removal of binder from internal regions of the assembly.

The debound assembly is thereafter sintered at a temperature and atmosphere sufficient to metallurgically bond and densify the metal particles. The ceramic powder is selected so that it does not substantially densify, melt, chemically bond to, or contaminate the metal bodies under the sintering conditions. Because the internal support structure is formed from the release material and may have a porous or discontinuous geometry, the support structure mechanically supports the metal-particle model material while allowing the metal bodies to contract during sintering. As a result, the metal bodies may densify with reduced distortion, slumping, cracking, or nonuniform shrinkage.

After sintering, the release material is removed from the assembly. Removal may leave a plurality of separate sintered metal parts, a set of interrelated metal parts, a multipart mechanism, a nested part set, a part with internal cavities, or a part assembly having gaps or clearances corresponding to the previously occupied release material. The release material may be recovered and optionally reused.

**Alternative Broad Claim**

24. A method comprising:  
 forming a green body by layerwise deposition of a first particulate feedstock and a second particulate feedstock, the first particulate feedstock comprising sinterable metal particles and the second particulate feedstock comprising ceramic release particles;  
 arranging the first particulate feedstock to define a plurality of metal part preforms;  
 arranging the second particulate feedstock to define both separable interfaces between the metal part preforms and a temporary internal support configured to maintain relative positioning of the metal part preforms;  
 thermally processing the green body to remove binder and sinter the metal particles; and  
 separating the ceramic release particles from the sintered metal particles,  
 wherein the temporary internal support permits the metal part preforms to undergo substantially uniform densification during the thermally processing.

A method comprising:

forming, by binder-based metal additive manufacturing, a green body comprising a metal powder bound with a binder, the green body defining a part having at least one hole, at least one support structure disposed in or adjacent to the at least one hole, and at least one release layer positioned between the part and the at least one support structure, the at least one release layer comprising a ceramic material;
